groups.title: Precious stones
groups.explanation: Each of these is a gemstone cut for jewellery.

groups.title: Wedding anniversaries
groups.explanation: Marriages are marked with these gifts, at one, five, twenty-five and fifty years.

groups.title: Pasta shapes
groups.explanation: These are dried pasta shapes, from quills to little bows.

sources.excerpt: Certain rocks (such as lapis lazuli, opal, and obsidian) and occasionally organic materials that are not minerals (such as amber, jet, and pearl) may also be used for jewelry and are therefore often considered to be gemstones as well.
Ruby is one of the most popular traditional jewelry gems and is very durable.
Ruby is one of the traditional cardinal gems, alongside amethyst, sapphire, emerald, and diamond.
Paper was recommended for the first anniversary, wood for the fifth anniversary and tin for the tenth anniversary.
Some significant anniversaries have names that suggest appropriate or traditional gifts, such as a silver or platinum jubilee.
Associating a wedding anniversary with precious metals such as "gold" (50 years) or "silver" (25 years) has been documented in Germanic countries since the 1500s.
It may have a simple shape like a thin cylinder (spaghetti), a sheet (lasagna), a tube (penne), or a grain, or be complex and three-dimensional.
Farfalle date back to the 16th century in the Lombardy and Emilia-Romagna regions of Italy.
Fusilli (Italian: [fuˈzilli]) are a variety of pasta from southern Italy, with a helical (corkscrew) or helicoidal shape, also known as rotini in the United States and Canada.
Rigatoni is a particularly favoured pasta shape in the south of Italy, especially in Sicily.

editorNotes: Ruby is the tile that fits twice, a red gemstone and the fortieth wedding anniversary; the anniversary group is complete with paper, wood, silver and gold, so ruby stays with the stones. Pearl and diamond anniversaries were considered and left out for that reason, and no pasta shape doubles as anything else here.
